summary: Reid Mayo's talk "Shift Left" provides a comprehensive syllabus for full-stack engineers to become AI engineers, requiring strong full-stack skills but no AI or ML background. Inspired by swyx's "The Rise of the AI Engineer" essay, Mayo emphasizes that full-stack engineers can now deploy useful AI solutions using foundational models without traditional ML expertise or costly upfront data collection. The syllabus is built around techniques from "The Art of Learning": staying focused, investing in fundamentals, and using ChatGPT as a Socratic private tutor. The bootcamp covers seven sections. Section one provides an LLM overview via Cohere's educational docs. Section two covers prompt engineering through the prompt engineering guide and learn prompting docs, noting that prompt quality also enhances fine-tuning training data. Section three focuses on OpenAI's docs and API reference for rapid prototyping. Section four dives into LangChain as the central glue framework for modular, scalable AI systems, recommending study of both Python and JavaScript docs plus real-world tutorials. Section five introduces evals as the AI equivalent of software tests, using OpenAI's eval framework for iterative improvement. Section six covers fine-tuning—starting with OpenAI's cookbook, then fine-tuning Meta's Llama 2 open-source model to match or beat OpenAI on target tasks, with a case study showing $19 vs. $244,000 cost savings. The efficient pattern is to prototype with OpenAI, gather usage data, then fine-tune cheaper open-source models for scaling. The final section recommends Fast.ai's deep learning course and Hugging Face's NLP course for advanced theory and training models from scratch.

sections.title: Introduction and Learning Methodology
sections.summary: Mayo introduces himself and the talk's purpose: a syllabus to transition full-stack engineers to AI engineers. Assumes strong full-stack background, zero AI/ML experience. Inspired by swyx's essay. Recommends techniques from "The Art of Learning": stay focused, invest in fundamentals, use ChatGPT as a Socratic tutor.

sections.title: Section 1: Overview to Large Language Models
sections.summary: Brief introduction to LLMs using Cohere's educational docs, founded by a Transformer architecture creator. Emphasizes reviewing module one in its entirety and pairing with Socratic method via ChatGPT.

sections.title: Section 2: Prompt Engineering
sections.summary: Covers prompt engineering despite its counterintuitive nature for engineers used to symbolic code logic. Notes that prompt quality also improves fine-tuning training data. Recommends prompt engineering guide by Elvis Saravia, learn prompting docs favored by OpenAI, and the graduate job classification case study.

sections.title: Section 3: OpenAI
sections.summary: OpenAI provides state-of-the-art models with high accessibility. Recommends reading OpenAI docs and API reference cover to cover, quickly reviewing cookbook examples. Notes practical limitations to address later regarding cost, latency, rate limiting, and privacy.

sections.title: Section 4: LangChain
sections.summary: LangChain is the application framework for organized, modular, scalable AI systems—integrating models, prompts, memory, RAG. Described as the glue layer for the AI ecosystem. Recommends executive summary by Command Bar, plain English technical guide, LangChain Python and JavaScript docs, GitHub codebase review, and Mayo Ocean's video tutorials.

sections.title: Section 5: Evaluating AI Models
sections.summary: Evals are the AI equivalent of software tests, providing a scientific process for evaluating changes before fine-tuning. Recommends OpenAI's eval cookbook and framework for writing custom evals. Notes that AI output requires creative eval approaches.

sections.title: Section 6: Fine-tuning
sections.summary: Covers OpenAI fine-tuning cookbook, then fine-tuning open-source models like Meta's Llama 2 to match or beat OpenAI on target tasks. Efficient pattern: prototype with OpenAI, gather data, fine-tune cheaper open-source model for scaling. OpenPipe case study shows $19 Llama 2 matching $244,000 OpenAI model. Addresses OpenAI limitations: cost, latency, rate limiting, privacy.

sections.title: Section 7: Advanced Study and Closing
sections.summary: Recommends deploying AI engineering skills in real world before advanced studies. Advanced resources: Fast.ai's practical deep learning course and Hugging Face's NLP course and docs for deep learning theory, further fine-tuning, and training models from scratch. Mayo directs audience to syllabus link and LinkedIn for questions.
